newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Accused in Ethiopia "Dergue" trial cross-examine.
newsitem.headline: Accused in Ethiopia "Dergue" trial cross-examine.

text.p: Former members of Ethiopia's military junta cross-examined prosecution witnesses on Thursday and one testified the main rebel group at the time had its own hit squad.
The 38-year-old prosecution witness, who under court rules cannot be identified, said he was a former operative for the main rebel Ethiopian People's Revolutionary Party (EPRP) in the 1970s.
"Yes, the EPRP had its own armed group and squads which had the power to kill its opponents or rehabilitate them and make them join the party," he said while being cross-examined by two accused.

Death squads in a terror campaign in 1977 and 1978 hunted down thousands of students from rival Marxist groups and other opposition organisations on behalf of the military junta, known as the "Dergue".

The government has charged more than 1,200 people suspected of involvement in the "Red Terror" campaign during the 17-year Marxist rule of dictator Mengistu Haile Mariam. They have yet to appear in court.
The trial of a total of 46 out of 71 former Dergue officials accused of genocide and crimes against humanity resumed on Thursday after a break of 15 days and was adjourned until next Tuesday.
The 25 others including Mengistu - in exile in Zimbabwe - are being tried in absentia. The 71 could be sentenced to death if found guilty.
Kassaye Aragaw, a former mayor and accused number 15, in a dramatic round of cross-examination asked the 38-year-old prosecution witness what he understood by the word "squad".
Witness: "a squad in EPRP terminology is an armed group with powers to eliminate or rehabilitate EPRP opponents."
Kassaye: "Can you confirm that EPRP had an armed wing?"
Kassaye: "Can you name persons or groups of persons who you think were murdered by EPRP hit squad?"
Witness: "Yes, I remember people talking, though I have not seen it personally, that Fikre Merid (a pro-Dergue revolutionary) and many other revolutionary guards were murdered by EPRP operatives."
The witness was cross-examined by two of the accused who had dismissed their court-appointed defence lawyers earlier.
Melaku Tefera, a former major and accused number 19, later also cross-examined a 53-year old witness who had said his brother was jailed, tortured and killed by the Dergue.
Melaku asked him whether he could name the person who killed his brother. The witness said he could not but the Dergue was responsible and Melaku was known as one of its most powerful members.
